record.paper_title: Orthogonal polynomials and approximation theory: some open problems
record.context_brief: Leading-coefficient ratios for disk orthogonal polynomials
record.original_question: Let {p_n} be the sequence of orthogonal polynomials associated with a measure supported on the unit disk, and let k_n denote the leading coefficient of p_n. Rakhmanov's theorem describes the asymptotic behavior of the analogous leading-coefficient ratios for orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. What is the behavior of the ratio k_n/k_{n+1} for orthogonal polynomials in the disk in an analogous setting?

evidence.quote: Behavior of the ratio of leading coefficients of orthogonal polynomials in the disc related to the Rakhmanov’s theorem concerning the analogue problem in the case of the unit circle

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a positive Borel measure with compact support contained in the closed unit disk $\overline{\mathbb{D}} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$, and assume $\mu$ has infinitely many points in its support. Let $\{p_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ be the sequence of polynomials obtained by orthonormalizing $\{1, z, z^2, \dots\}$ with respect to the inner product
$$\langle f, g \rangle_\mu = \int_{\overline{\mathbb{D}}} f(z) \overline{g(z)} \, d\mu(z),$$
so that $p_n(z) = k_n z^n + \text{(lower order terms)}$ with $k_n > 0$.

Recall Rakhmanov's theorem for the unit circle: if $\mu$ is a measure on the unit circle $\partial \mathbb{D}$ whose absolutely continuous part $\mu'$ satisfies $\mu' > 0$ almost everywhere on $\partial \mathbb{D}$, then the ratio $k_n / k_{n+1}$ of the leading coefficients of the corresponding orthonormal polynomials tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of the ratio $k_n / k_{n+1}$ as $n \to \infty$ for orthonormal polynomials associated with a measure $\mu$ supported on the unit disk $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$, in a setting analogous to the hypothesis of Rakhmanov's theorem (for instance, when the two-dimensional absolutely continuous part of $\mu$ is positive almost everywhere on $\mathbb{D}$). In particular, identify natural conditions on $\mu$ under which $\lim_{n \to \infty} k_n/k_{n+1}$ exists, and compute its value.
artifact.status_search_result: Rakhmanov's classical theorem on the unit circle and several extensions (matrix-valued, varying measures, Denisov-type) are well documented. A direct analogue for the ratio of leading coefficients of orthonormal polynomials with respect to area-type measures on the unit disk does not appear definitively settled in the search results, and no specific resolution under analogous hypotheses on the disk was located. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics for the ratio of leading coefficients of orthonormal polynomials on the unit circle
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Rakhmanov-type results for k_n/k_{n+1} on the unit circle.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the circle setting that the disk problem seeks to extend.

status_evidence.title: Rakhmanov's theorem for orthogonal matrix polynomials on the unit circle
status_evidence.snippet: Matrix-valued analogue of Rakhmanov's theorem on the circle.
status_evidence.claim: Shows extensions exist on the circle, but does not address the disk case.
